characteristic_extranodal_sites: GI tract (lymphomatous polyposis — colon and small bowel; often occult)
sanctuary_sites: CNS (blastoid variant has higher CNS relapse risk)

biomarkers.name: t(11;14)(q13;q32) IGH-CCND1 → cyclin D1 overexpression
biomarkers.clinical_use: Defining event in the great majority of cases. Cyclin D1 IHC is diagnostic in most cases. Rare cyclin D1-negative MCL exists (often with CCND2 or CCND3 rearrangements)

biomarkers.name: SOX11
biomarkers.clinical_use: Usually positive in classic nodal MCL. SOX11-negative cases are enriched in leukaemic non-nodal MCL, which is often more indolent and may be suitable for watch-and-wait in selected patients

biomarkers.name: CD5+, CD19+, CD20+ (bright), CD23-, CD200-
biomarkers.clinical_use: Typical immunophenotype helps distinguish from CLL, although a subset of MCL may show CD23 positivity and/or dim CD200 expression

biomarkers.name: TP53 mutation
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very adverse; associated with poor outcomes after standard immunochemotherapy. Also associated with inferior outcomes with covalent BTK inhibitors; cellular therapy or clinical trial is often preferred in eligible patients

biomarkers.name: Ki-67 index
biomarkers.clinical_use: Higher Ki-67 is adverse; Ki-67 ≥30% is commonly used as a high-risk threshold and is incorporated into MIPI-c/MIPI-b biologic models. Blastoid/pleomorphic variants often have very high Ki-67

biomarkers.name: MIPI / MIPI-b (biological)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Age, ECOG, LDH, WBC; biologic variants incorporate Ki-67 (commonly termed MIPI-c). Guides risk stratification and treatment intensity

biomarkers.name: BTK inhibitor response (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, pirtobrutinib)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Established standard in relapsed/refractory disease. Pirtobrutinib (non-covalent BTK inhibitor) is active after covalent BTK inhibitor failure

biomarkers.name: BTK C481S mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: A recognized mechanism of resistance to covalent BTK inhibitors; pirtobrutinib can retain activity after such resistance

biomarkers.name: CD19
biomarkers.clinical_use: Brexucabtagene autoleucel (ZUMA-2) — CD19 CAR-T approved for R/R MCL after prior BTK inhibitor exposure/failure

biomarkers.name: BCL2
biomarkers.clinical_use: Venetoclax has activity alone and in combination in R/R MCL, but BCL2 IHC expression is not a validated predictive biomarker for routine selection

biomarkers.name: Blastoid / pleomorphic variant
biomarkers.clinical_use: Aggressive; high Ki-67; associated with higher CNS relapse risk

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Monomorphic small to medium-sized B cells with irregular nuclei effacing mantle zone; multiple growth patterns
variants: classic MCL (mantle zone, nodular, diffuse growth)
leukaemic non-nodal MCL (often SOX11-, indolent, better prognosis)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not formally graded; blastoid/pleomorphic are aggressive variants

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: BCR signalling dependency contributes to BTK inhibitor sensitivity; anti-apoptotic dependence contributes to venetoclax activity; CD19 CAR-T (brexucabtagene) is established after BTK inhibitor failure
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Multiple architectural patterns (mantle zone, nodular, diffuse); lymphomatous polyposis in GI tract

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Naive-like B cells of pre-germinal centre stage (mantle zone B cells) with t(11;14)/CCND1 rearrangement
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Mantle zone B-cell differentiation with characteristic CD5+, CD19+, CD20 bright+, CD10-, CD23- immunophenotype; SOX11 nuclear expression is characteristic of typical MCL
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Two biologic forms are recognized: typical MCL (usually SOX11+, often IGHV-unmutated, more aggressive, nodal-predominant) vs leukaemic non-nodal MCL (often SOX11-, often IGHV-mutated, more indolent — consistent with a memory-like/post-germinal-centre program); TP53 alterations drive aggressive behaviour and treatment resistance
